Associate Product Manager — Digital Ordering

About Us
LimeTray builds digital ordering products for some of the world's largest restaurant chains. Domino's, Burger King, Tim Hortons, Jollibee, and Wingstop run their customer-facing ordering experiences on our platform — web, native app, QR dine-in, and self-ordering kiosks — across India, UAE, and Qatar.

The Role
We're hiring an Associate Product Manager to own our digital ordering product group. You'll work directly with the founder and engineering team to understand how each ordering surface is performing, where customers are dropping off, and what to build or fix next. No layers, no hand-holding on what to look at — you bring the view.

Key Responsibilities
• Own the product roadmap across web, app, QR dine-in, and kiosk ordering surfaces
• Analyse funnel data across live customer stores and identify where orders are being lost
• Write specs that engineering can execute without follow-up questions
• Sit on calls with enterprise customers and translate their needs into product decisions
• Define and track success metrics for each ordering surface
• Work with engineering to ship, iterate, and improve continuously
Qualifications
• 2-3 years in consumer product or growth, ideally in food delivery, ecommerce, or quick commerce
• Comfortable pulling data and forming a point of view — funnel analysis, drop-off patterns, usage metrics
• Hands-on with product analytics tools like Mixpanel, Amplitude, or Clevertap
• Writes clearly, thinks independently, moves fast
• Familiarity with AI tools like Claude, Lovable, or similar is a strong plus
What You Get
• Direct ownership of products used daily by customers of Domino's, Burger King, and Tim Hortons
• Work directly with the founder — short feedback loops, fast decisions
• Breadth most APMs don't get until they're 5 years in

372b07c04bc9b3c2.description: This role is not about building a model in isolation. It's about taking a client's vague business problem, making it measurable, and turning it into a system their people rely on to make a decision. When that happens, you can point to the decision that changed because of your work. Few roles let you see your impact that clearly. You own the problem end to end: framing it, engineering the features, modeling it, proving it moved the number that matters, and getting it into a form the client actually uses. Predictive analytics, decision intelligence, and the systems that put insight where decisions are made. That's your territory. **The work:** * Shape a client's real challenge into a problem we can solve * Engineer features and build models tied to outcomes that matter: productivity, better decisions, lower cost * Design the experiments and metrics that show a value slice delivered * Build the decision-intelligence and BI deliverables (PowerBI, Tableau) that surface insight at the point of decision * Explain your reasoning, and your trade-offs, to client stakeholders who don't work in math **Where your work ends.** You consume the data the Data Engineer serves; you don't build the pipelines. You own the model and the insight; when a model needs to run as a hardened production or agentic system, you hand it to the AI Engineer, and you rely on the Software Engineer for any custom application interface. Your ownership is the modeling and the decision it drives. **What success looks like:** * A client decision measurably improves, and you can prove which number moved * Models are validated and honest about their uncertainty * Insight lands where decisions are actually made, not in a report no one opens * Every value slice you deliver carries a metric that shows it worked The stack we work in today: Python with Scikit-Learn and PyTorch; NLP and computer vision where the problem calls for it; Neo4j Graph Data Science for graph-based analytics; and PowerBI or Tableau for decision support. Beyond the tools, you should be able to package, deploy, and monitor your own work, because a model that never ships helps no one, and communicate clearly with client stakeholders. In a consulting setting that communication often matters more than the modeling. **About The Strong AI, and how we work** The Strong AI is an end-to-end AI implementation partner. Clients come to us because most organizations can run an AI experiment, but few can turn it into a system their business depends on. We close that gap. We don't hand over slideware or a notebook; we build systems that work inside a client's business, and where they want it, we run them. You'll work across engagements and industries, on different problems and often different stacks. We're technology-agnostic: the problem and the client's environment choose the tools, so treat any stack we list as the ground we work on today, not a gate. **Across all roles, we ask for the same way of working:** * Real software. Tested, reviewed, versioned code the next person, or the client's team, can pick up. * MLOps mindset. A model's life starts at deployment. Monitoring, retraining, drift, and rollback are handled before anything breaks. * Systems thinking. You see both the value slice and the whole it compounds into. * Quality and security, owned by you. Designed in from the first decision, not inspected in at the end. Everyone builds to the highest standard. * Built for handover. Clear code and docs the client's own team can understand, operate, and take over.
